title: exFAT cold-tail extension re-enters an inode write guard
mechanism: ExfatInode::write_at calls PageCache::resize under inner.write(). For an unaligned old size the extension branch runs fill_zeros on the tail page, which commits an uncached page through the backend, and the exFAT backend submit_read_bio takes inner.read() on the same non-reentrant RwMutex, so the writer deadlocks on itself while holding the fs lock.
contract: write(2)/pwrite(2): an extending write to a regular file returns a count or an error and never blocks forever on a lock held by the calling task.
observed: After remounting exFAT so the tail page of a 100-byte file was uncached, pwrite64(fd, buf, 16, 100) did not return within 10 s and the guest had to be killed by the outer timeout. Cached-tail exFAT and remounted ext2 controls returned 16.

repro.how_to_run: Build test_bugCR-2_exfat_resize_tailclear.c statically with -pthread as /init, attach fresh ext2 (/dev/vda) and exFAT (/dev/vdb) images, boot with an outer timeout. 'pwrite64 DID NOT RETURN' and CR2-CLAIM-A: REPRODUCED mean the bug fired.
repro.runtime_status: REPRODUCED at 604948581 (01b CR-2, SMP=2, Level 0, guest ran as root for umount/mount)

caveats: Raw CR-2 was a documentation-contradiction finding that confirmation turned into a runtime deadlock. The guest ran as root to umount/mount for the cold cache. Unprivileged cold-cache setup was not independently established. Only the buffered path ran, and write_direct_at was not tested. The AST-11 fix branch leaves this deadlock in place.
